concepts.quote: StdIn is a variable that holds all the numbers, like an array.
concepts.why: StdIn is a library of static methods that read tokens from a stream. It is not a variable that stores all the input values.

concepts.way: misconception: A variable can contain more than one value.
concepts.quote: a variable that holds all the numbers
concepts.why: The answer says one variable holds many values, but a Java variable holds exactly one value at a time.
The answer does not mention the isEmpty() loop or how it reads and processes values.

concepts.quote: holds all the numbers, like an array
concepts.why: Treating input as stored values you can look back at, like an array, contradicts the rule that a stream is used up one value at a time.
